segments.title: 第78章 真正的班長
segments.content:
Chapter 78: The True Class President

QQ groups are a very magical thing.

Once some highly viral gossip appears on the internet, a fission-like reaction occurs within QQ groups.

One person tells ten, ten tell a hundred.

And in the past few days, the matter of "a certain web novel author actually composing an original song for their entertainment-focused novel" had also been turned into a viral anecdote, spreading rapidly through web novel-related QQ groups.

At first, it was just author groups and reader groups. Later, it slowly spread to some gaming and anime groups, and more and more people came to listen to "Annual Ring" after hearing about it.

The number of followers for "I'm Really Not a Star," which was originally only twenty thousand, also rose to thirty thousand in just a few short days.

Unfortunately, most of the interested people, even if they learned the name of the book "I'm Really Not a Star," would at most search for it on a pirate site.

Many web novel readers probably didn't even know what "Qidian" was, nor did they have any concept of pirated versus official versions.

But even so, for Li Luo, the surge of readers brought by this wave of traffic still had many benefits.

At the very least, his average subscriptions were rising quickly.

At this rate, there was a good chance he could break three thousand average subscriptions this month and earn the electronic badge symbolizing a "Boutique" work.

Once he could step into this stage, it would symbolize that his web novel's quality had truly reached a respectable level, and he could start to consider the feasibility of writing full-time.

But for a high school student, Li Luo didn't need to think that far ahead yet.

And the song "Annual Ring," under the impact of this traffic, had only spread within a limited, small circle.

To say it wasn't popular, an unknown little figure wrote a new song, and in just a few days, its plays on a single platform had exceeded several hundred thousand.

But to say it was popular, compared to those songs that had truly exploded, there was a substantial gap.

In any case, it was far from the popularity "Annual Ring" had in his previous life.

For Li Luo, this also happened to confirm one point.

For a song, having a high quality was a prerequisite, but just how popular it could ultimately become still depended on how much traffic and buzz it received.

It could be the same song with a hundred million plays, or with several hundred thousand. Sometimes, it was really hard to understand the logic behind a song's explosion in popularity.

But what Li Luo didn't know was that his song had not only landed on major music platforms but had also been recommended internally for a TV series that Huayue Film and Television was preparing to produce, serving as a candidate for the theme song and currently undergoing the selection process.

When the time came to Saturday, Li Luo arrived at his school classroom as usual.

However, no teachers held classes on Saturdays, nor was there a morning self-study session. Students could arrive half an hour later and then have four consecutive self-study periods.

Simply put, it was the time arranged by the school for students to do their homework on the weekend.

If the head teacher had any matters to attend to, they would also handle them during these periods.

Many students might not have the motivation to do their homework diligently after going home for the weekend.

So the idea of the academic affairs office at the First Affiliated High School, which was responsible for the schedule, was very simple.

With Friday evening's self-study, plus Saturday's four self-study periods, and Sunday evening's self-study, students should be able to get their homework done.

For the remaining time, Saturday afternoon was for club activities. The kids would go home in the evening to reunite with their parents, rest and have fun during the day on Sunday, and then return to school in the evening.

The arrangement was quite perfect.

However, early this morning, as soon as Li Luo walked into the classroom, he noticed many people gathered in front of the teacher's desk.

Standing in the middle was Kong Junxiang, holding a list in his hand.

Li Luo walked to his seat, put down his schoolbag, and asked Yan Zhusheng, who had arrived earlier, only to find out that the results of the placement exam were out.

With a sense of curiosity, Li Luo went up to the desk and glanced at the results sheet in Kong Junxiang's hand.

After scanning it, he nodded and walked away, having a clear understanding of his scores.

Chinese 107, Math 99, English 110, total score 316, ranking 14th in the class and 328th in the whole school.

On one hand, 160 top students from the key classes had joined the fray this time.

On the other hand, Li Luo didn't know the test questions in advance. Relying solely on his memory palace, he lost quite a few points in math.

As for Chinese and English, although his scores were not as good as in the high school entrance exam, they were more or less the same, so the impact wasn't too significant.

If the 160 students from the key classes were excluded, his school-wide rank would be 168th. Compared to his 86th place in the entire district for the entrance exam, it was a drop of over eighty places, which was still within an acceptable range.

However, if he wanted to get into Qianjiang University smoothly in the college entrance exam, this ranking was far from enough.

He had to at least get into the top hundred in the school, breaking into the rankings dominated by the key classes, to have a glimmer of hope.

Fortunately, there was still a lot of time, and he could improve slowly.

"You're not going to look?" Li Luo asked, turning his head toward Yan Zhusheng after returning to his seat.

"The teacher will definitely announce them later, I'm not in a hurry." Yan Zhusheng shook her head, then added, "Besides, don't you have a good memory? Can you remember it all with just one look?"

"Heh." Li Luo smiled and said, propping up his chin, "You got 318 points, two points higher than me. 11th in the class, 304th in the school."

Yan Zhusheng's Chinese was 106 and Math was 97, both slightly lower than Li Luo's, but her English score was 115, which was very high. One could only say it was to be expected from someone who had lived abroad.

As for Li Luo's several old classmates, Jin Yuting's rank in the class was not bad, around thirtieth.

Without science dragging her down, looking at just the three main subjects, Jin Yuting's foundation wasn't too bad.

Xu Yinghuan scored 25th, a middle-of-the-road level, which was a stable performance for her.

As for Shao Heqi... without science, his main point-booster subject, his total score this time was 315, one point less than Li Luo again, ranking him 15th in the class.

The occasional glances he shot at Li Luo were slightly dejected. Seeing the other boy remain silent, the beautiful comeback scene in his mind ultimately failed to materialize.

However, Shao Heqi was now full of confidence and ambition, eagerly looking forward to the midterm exams to achieve a grand reversal!

After all, in Shao Heqi's view, Li Luo's level in the three main subjects had clearly declined compared to the high school entrance exam.

Especially in math, it was obvious he hadn't diligently reviewed to maintain his level during the summer vacation and was immediately exposed.

Shao Heqi knew very well that Li Luo had only scored 142 in science on the entrance exam, while he, Shao Heqi, had scored a full 162!

If science were included, he would have definitely surpassed Li Luo.

So although he was silent for now, Shao Heqi's mind had already begun to fantasize about a beautiful future.

Li Luo didn't care what Shao Heqi was thinking; he just checked the scores of other classmates.

For example, Zhu Yufei and Zhang Guohuang. Although those two jokers were always fooling around and amusing everyone in class, their grades were actually very good.

After all, they were people who had once participated in the independent recruitment of the First Affiliated High School. Although they weren't selected, they could still maintain a top-five rank in their parallel class.

And the first place in the class this time was that animal lover, Lu Jiahao, who was also the math class representative Li Luo had previously recommended.

Second place went to Shi Yanran, who had once run for class president.

They're all true academic powerhouses... Li Luo looked at these people who could score over 330 out of a possible 360 and couldn't help but click his tongue in admiration.

If he didn't study seriously, even with the memory palace, he couldn't get such high scores. He had no idea how these people studied.

Thinking of this, Li Luo's gaze fell on the chubby Shi Yanran in the front row, and he secretly cheered her on.

Shi Yanran! I have high hopes for you. You have to remember to go up on stage during the class committee election later!

And Hua Xiuxiu!

Li Luo looked to the other side.

Even though you only ranked 22nd in the class this time, everyone has witnessed your abilities. You can't get stage fright during the class president election later!

As he was thinking this, the bell for the first self-study period had already rung.

Kong Junxiang called for everyone to take their seats, posted the results sheet he was holding onto the wall, and then said, "The results of the placement exam are just a reference for everyone."

"After all, after entering high school, each subject will have new knowledge systems for you to learn and absorb."

"Your grades will also see great changes."

"So whether you did well or not, don't overthink it. The most important thing is to have the right attitude and embrace the student life that follows."

Kong Junxiang didn't dwell on the placement exam results. After a few brief words, he changed the subject, "Next, let's take care of the unfinished business from the start of school."

"Previously, our class elected a class president, a vice president, and two physical education committee members."

"This time, not only will we elect the remaining class officers, but we will also hold re-elections for the four positions mentioned above."

"Same old rules. Students who are interested can voluntarily come up on stage to run. I will write the relevant positions on the blackboard."

As he spoke, Kong Junxiang had already started writing on the blackboard, listing all the positions like Class President, Youth League Secretary, Academic Committee Member, and Labor Committee Member.

"OK." Kong Junxiang tossed the chalk into the chalk box on the desk, then clapped his hands and said, "Now, I'll leave the stage to you all."

More than half an hour later, the first self-study period was nearing its end.

Li Luo sat in the back row, momentarily falling into silence.

"Alright, the above are the results of this election." Kong Junxiang said with a smile as he wrote the names of the students corresponding to each position on the blackboard. "Because no one ran for class president this time, our class president will continue to be Li Luo."

"Li Luo, it seems everyone is quite satisfied with you as the class president."

"In the time to come, you must lead our Class Eight well and do a good job serving everyone."

Hearing this, Li Luo's mouth twitched, and he forced a smile, "Okay, Teacher Kong."

Then, his eyes fell on Hua Xiuxiu in the front row, filled with a sense of disappointment.

You girl!

Where's that drive and unwillingness to admit defeat you had at the beginning of the semester?

You have no competitive spirit at all!

You've grown addicted to this vice president position, haven't you?

Your class president is very disappointed in you!

(End of Chapter)
